record.paper_title: Open Problems in K-Stability of Fano Varieties
record.original_question: Is the Frobenius volume Fvol(x, X) of a singularity always an algebraic number?

evidence.quote: Problem 44. Is Fvol(x, X) an algebraic number?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X, x)$ be the germ of a Noetherian local ring of positive characteristic $p > 0$ at a closed point $x$, assumed to be an $F$-finite normal local domain with an isolated non-regular point at $x$ (or more generally a klt-type singularity in characteristic $p$). For each positive integer $e$, let $F^e \colon X \to X$ denote the $e$-th iterate of the absolute Frobenius endomorphism, and consider the asymptotic invariant
$$\mathrm{Fvol}(x, X) \;=\; \lim_{e \to \infty} \frac{1}{p^{e \cdot \dim X}} \cdot \mathrm{(Frobenius\ length/colength\ invariant\ at\ }x\mathrm{)},$$
the Frobenius volume of the singularity $(x \in X)$, defined as the appropriate normalization of the Frobenius pushforward / splitting data attached to the singularity (so that, e.g., for a smooth point $\mathrm{Fvol}(x, X) = 1$).

Question: Is $\mathrm{Fvol}(x, X)$ always an algebraic number, for every such singularity $(x \in X)$?
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution was located. The algebraicity of Frobenius-type singularity invariants (such as Hilbert–Kunz multiplicity, F-signature, and the Frobenius volume) is a well-known open question in the theory of F-singularities; even the rationality of the Hilbert–Kunz multiplicity remains famously unresolved, and no source found establishes algebraicity of $\mathrm{Fvol}(x, X)$ in general.

status_evidence.title: A guided tour to normalized volume
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of normalized volume of klt singularities and related Frobenius/local volume invariants; algebraicity questions remain open in general.
status_evidence.claim: Algebraicity of local/Frobenius volume invariants is not established in general.

status_evidence.title: Measuring Singularities with Frobenius: The Basics
status_evidence.snippet: Overview of Frobenius-based singularity invariants; rationality/algebraicity of these invariants (e.g. Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity) remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Standard Frobenius invariants are not known to be algebraic numbers in general.
